steps.title: AO6 Requirement
steps.body: Accurate and effective punctuation isn't just about correctness - it's about using punctuation deliberately to create effects and control your reader's experience.

steps.title: Tip
steps.body: The colon acts like a spotlight, directing attention to what comes next. Use it to make important statements stand out.

steps.title: Think of it this way
steps.body: A semi-colon is stronger than a comma but weaker than a full stop. It shows ideas are connected but distinct.

steps.title: Dash Tip
steps.body: An em dash (—) is longer than a hyphen (-). In exams, you can use two hyphens (--) if you can't make an em dash.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Rewrite this sentence using a colon for emphasis: "She wanted one thing only, revenge." | Rewrite using a semi-colon: "The door slammed. She jumped." | Add a dash for dramatic effect: "He opened the box and saw something unexpected."

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: She wanted one thing only: revenge. | The door slammed; she jumped. | He opened the box—and saw something unexpected.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use colons for dramatic effect in creative writing Semi-colons show sophistication - use them to link related ideas Dashes are more dramatic than commas - use for emphasis Ellipsis builds suspense in descriptive and narrative writing Check speech punctuation carefully - it's easy to lose marks here Don't overuse exclamation marks - they lose impact
